nodes.statement:
Let $G \sim G_{n, \frac{p}{D}}$ and let $S \subseteq W$ be a set of at most
	$Dn \exp\left(-(\log n)^\alpha/12\right)$ vertices
	chosen independently from the edges between $U$ and $W$.
	Then \aas no vertex in $U$ has more than $\frac{1}{2}(\log n)^\beta$ neighbours in~$S$.
assumptions: $S \subseteq W$ be a set of at most $Dn \exp\left(-(\log n)^\alpha/12\right)$ vertices chosen independently from the edges between $U$ and $W$
conclusions: \aas no vertex in $U$ has more than $\frac{1}{2}(\log n)^\beta$ neighbours in~$S$
nodes.label: lm:no-removal-impact

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 18
nodes.statement_short: Chernoff upper tail for the number of neighbours in the small set S, then union bound over U.

nodes.name: σ(u) is a binomial count
nodes.statement:
Let $u \in U$ and let $\sigma(u)$ denote the number of neighbours of~$u$ in~$S$.
	Observe that $\sigma(u)$~is a sum of $\abs{S}$~independent indicator variables.
nodes.statement_short: σ(u) is a binomial count

nodes.name: Expected σ(u) is tiny
nodes.statement:
We have that
	$$
	\mathbb{E}[\sigma(u)] = \frac{p}{D}\abs{S} 
	< 2C^2 (\log n)^\alpha \exp\left(-(\log n)^\alpha/12\right).
	$$
nodes.statement_short: Expected σ(u) is tiny

nodes.name: Fix h and δ
nodes.statement:
Let us fix a positive constant $h$ such that 
	$\mu := \mathbb{E}[\sigma(u)] < \exp\left(-4h(\log n)^\alpha\right)$,
	and let $\delta := \frac{(\log n)^\beta}{2\mu}-1 \in \omega(1)$.
nodes.statement_short: Fix h and δ

nodes.name: Chernoff upper tail
nodes.statement_short: Chernoff upper tail

nodes.name: Union bound over U
nodes.statement: Applying the union bound over all~$O(n)$~vertices $u \in U$ concludes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Union bound over U

nodes.name: No removal cascade
nodes.statement:
Let $G \sim G_{n, \frac{p}{D}}$ and let $S \subseteq W$ be a set of at most
	$Dn \exp\left(-(\log n)^\alpha/12\right)$ vertices
	chosen independently from the edges between $U$ and $W$.
	Then \aas every vertex in~$U$ with at least $(\log n)^\beta$ neighbours in~$W$
	has at least $(\log n)^\gamma$ neighbors in $W \setminus S$.
assumptions: $S \subseteq W$ be a set of at most $Dn \exp\left(-(\log n)^\alpha/12\right)$ vertices chosen independently from the edges between $U$ and $W$
conclusions: \aas every vertex in~$U$ with at least $(\log n)^\beta$ neighbours in~$W$ has at least $(\log n)^\gamma$ neighbors in $W \setminus S$
nodes.label: lm:no-removal-cascade

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 7
nodes.statement:
A vertex with at least $(\log n)^\beta$ neighbours in~$W$
	but fewer than $(\log n)^\gamma$ neighbours in~$W \setminus S$
	must have more than $(\log n)^\beta - (\log n)^\gamma > \frac{1}{2}(\log n)^\beta$ neighbours in~$S$.
	By~\cref{lm:no-removal-impact},
	there are \aas no such vertices.
nodes.statement_short: A violating vertex would have over (log n)^β/2 neighbours in S, excluded by Lemma 18.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 15
nodes.statement:
For every $i \in [C]$, let $B_i \subseteq V_i$ contains those vertices that have fewer than $(\log n)^\beta$ neighbours in~$V_{i+1}$ in \emph{at least one} of the $D$ graphs $G_1, G_2, \ldots, G_D$. Set $V'_i:=V_i\setminus B_i$.
	
	By~\cref{lm:few-sleepers}, \aas
	each $B_i$ has size at most $D n \exp\left(-(\log n)^\alpha/12\right)  \in o(n)$.
	The choice of $B_{i+1}$ is independent of edges between $V_{i}$ and $V_{i+1}$,
	hence we can apply \cref{lm:no-removal-cascade} and the union bound
	over all $D$ graphs to obtain
	that \aas in each graph every vertex in $V'_i$ has at least
	$(\log n)^\gamma$ neighbours in $V'_{i+1} = V_{i+1} \setminus B_{i+1}$.
nodes.statement_short: Remove vertices with few neighbours in the next sector; Lemma 17 bounds removals and Corollary 7 rules out cascades.

nodes.name: Define removed sets B_i and V'_i
nodes.statement: For every $i \in [C]$, let $B_i \subseteq V_i$ contains those vertices that have fewer than $(\log n)^\beta$ neighbours in~$V_{i+1}$ in \emph{at least one} of the $D$ graphs $G_1, G_2, \ldots, G_D$. Set $V'_i:=V_i\setminus B_i$.
nodes.statement_short: Define removed sets B_i and V'_i

nodes.name: Lemma 17: few removals
nodes.statement:
By~\cref{lm:few-sleepers}, \aas
	each $B_i$ has size at most $D n \exp\left(-(\log n)^\alpha/12\right)  \in o(n)$.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 17: few removals

nodes.name: Independence lets Corollary 7 rule out cascades
nodes.statement:
The choice of $B_{i+1}$ is independent of edges between $V_{i}$ and $V_{i+1}$,
	hence we can apply \cref{lm:no-removal-cascade} and the union bound
	over all $D$ graphs to obtain
	that \aas in each graph every vertex in $V'_i$ has at least
	$(\log n)^\gamma$ neighbours in $V'_{i+1} = V_{i+1} \setminus B_{i+1}$.
nodes.statement_short: Independence lets Corollary 7 rule out cascades

nodes.name: Binomial tail bound
nodes.statement:
Let $X \sim \operatorname{Bin}(N, q)$ for some~$N \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}$ and $2Nq \leq 1$.
	Then 
	\[
	\mathbb{P}[X \geq k] \leq  2 (Nq)^k .
	\]
conclusions: \mathbb{P}[X \geq k] \leq  2 (Nq)^k .
nodes.label: lm:binomial-bound

nodes.name: Proof of Claim 1
nodes.statement_short: Bound binomial coefficients by N^i and sum the geometric series.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 16
nodes.statement:
By \cref{lm:binomial-bound}, the probability that any fixed vertex in $W$ has three or more neighbors in~$A$ is at most
	\[
	2 \left((\log n)^{C \gamma} \frac{p}{D}\right)^3
	=
	2\left(\frac{C (\log n)^{C \gamma + \alpha}}{n}\right)^3
	\in o(1/n^2).
	\]
	
	Thus, by the union bound, the probability that any vertex in~$W$ has three or more neighbors in $A$ is in $o(1/n)$.
	
	Similarly, the probability that any fixed vertex in~$W$ has two or more neighbors in~$A$ is at most
	\[
	2 \left((\log n)^{C \gamma}\frac{p}{D}\right)^2.
	\]
	Applying \cref{lm:binomial-bound} again gives that the probability of having two or more vertices in~$W$ that each have two or more neighbors in~$A$ is at most
	\begin{align*}
	2\left(|W| \cdot 2\left((\log n)^{C \gamma} \frac{p}{D}\right)^2\right)^2 &\leq
	2\left(2 \ceil*{\frac{n}{C}} \left((\log n)^{C \gamma} \frac{p}{D}\right)^2\right)^2
	\\ &= 8 \ceil*{\frac{n}{C}}^2 \left((\log n)^{C\gamma} \frac{p}{D}\right)^4 
	\in o(1/n)\,. \qedhere
	\end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Claim 1 bounds per-vertex collision probabilities; union bounds over W.

nodes.name: Claim 1: triple collisions at a vertex are unlikely
nodes.statement:
By \cref{lm:binomial-bound}, the probability that any fixed vertex in $W$ has three or more neighbors in~$A$ is at most
	\[
	2 \left((\log n)^{C \gamma} \frac{p}{D}\right)^3
	=
	2\left(\frac{C (\log n)^{C \gamma + \alpha}}{n}\right)^3
	\in o(1/n^2).
	\]
nodes.statement_short: Claim 1: triple collisions at a vertex are unlikely

nodes.name: Union bound over W
nodes.statement: Thus, by the union bound, the probability that any vertex in~$W$ has three or more neighbors in $A$ is in $o(1/n)$.
nodes.statement_short: Union bound over W

nodes.name: Probability of a double collision at a vertex
nodes.statement:
Similarly, the probability that any fixed vertex in~$W$ has two or more neighbors in~$A$ is at most
	\[
	2 \left((\log n)^{C \gamma}\frac{p}{D}\right)^2.
	\]
nodes.statement_short: Probability of a double collision at a vertex

nodes.name: At most one double collision w.h.p.
nodes.statement:
Applying \cref{lm:binomial-bound} again gives that the probability of having two or more vertices in~$W$ that each have two or more neighbors in~$A$ is at most
	\begin{align*}
	2\left(|W| \cdot 2\left((\log n)^{C \gamma} \frac{p}{D}\right)^2\right)^2 &\leq
	2\left(2 \ceil*{\frac{n}{C}} \left((\log n)^{C \gamma} \frac{p}{D}\right)^2\right)^2
	\\ &= 8 \ceil*{\frac{n}{C}}^2 \left((\log n)^{C\gamma} \frac{p}{D}\right)^4 
	\in o(1/n)\,. \qedhere
	\end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: At most one double collision w.h.p.
